The trip record's own derived contact check reports message_count 0 and obligation_met false, so the message limb fails outright and the 5.00 SGD fee must be voided with a FULL_REFUND of the fee charged and no driver compensation.

The chat log for this trip carries exactly one entry, and it is the rider's own message 'Coming down now, sorry', sent at 12:21:50 and delivered at 12:21:53 — forty seconds AFTER the driver cancelled at 12:21:10. There is no driver message at any point in the log, before or after the cancellation, so nothing in the record can satisfy the message limb of POL-NS-23.

The driver's own account is 'I called two times, no answer.' That asserts calls and nothing else: it does not claim, and the record nowhere shows, that any in-app message was ever sent to the rider. The two in-app calls at 12:17:55 and 12:19:40 (unanswered, 20 s and 18 s) establish the call limb of POL-NS-23 and only the call limb.

The rider's admission that his phone was on silent explains only why the two calls rang out; it does not touch the separate requirement that the driver also message him in the app. POL-NS-23 is conjunctive — a ringing call is not a message — and on this record the rider was left with no in-app notice of where the driver was waiting or that he was about to be cancelled on.

The rider sent 'Coming down now, sorry' forty seconds after the driver cancelled, which shows he was responding and on his way down rather than lost to the trip. A single in-app message from the driver, which POL-NS-23 requires and which costs nothing, would have reached him before the cancellation instead of after it.

ruling.explanation:
Rider R-58651 and driver D-14699: this is a NO_SHOW_CHARGE dispute over the 5.00 SGD cancellation fee on TRP-05053. I find for the rider; the 5.00 SGD fee is refunded in full.

What is common ground, and what I accept. The driver arrived at the pickup at 12:15:30: the trip record's auto-arrival is corroborated by EV-GPS-05053, whose nearest fix to Block 662 is 3.07 m away at 6 m reported accuracy, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius POL-NS-21 sets. The trip was on-demand with no scheduled pickup time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait ran from arrival and expired at 12:20:30; the driver cancelled at 12:21:10, 340 s after arrival. The arrival and wait prerequisites of POL-NS-21 are met, and both advocates correctly say so.

The case turns on POL-NS-23, the driver's contact obligation, which is conjunctive: before cancelling for no-show the driver must have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call, both before cancellation. The call limb is met — EV-TRIP-05053 records two in-app calls placed by the driver at 12:17:55 (rang 20 s) and 12:19:40 (rang 18 s), unanswered, and both the driver's own statement ('I called two times, no answer') and the rider's account ('He did call') confirm the calls.

The message limb is not met. EV-CHAT-05053 contains exactly one entry in the whole trip, and it is the rider's 'Coming down now, sorry', sent at 12:21:50 — forty seconds after the driver cancelled at 12:21:10. There is no driver message before or after the cancellation; the trip record's own contact check records message_count 0 and obligation_met false, and the driver's advocate properly concedes that no in-app message was sent. POL-NS-23 provides that if either limb is missing the fee is voided and the rider is not charged. The message limb is missing, so the fee cannot stand. The rider's admission that his phone was on silent explains only why the two calls rang unanswered; it does not supply the separate message the clause requires. Nor does it matter that the rider was still on his way down (his message about coming down was sent after the driver had already given up): the obligation sits on the driver and is unconditional.

For that reason I do not reach the driver's submission that the fee stands under POL-NS-22 and passes to him as compensation. That submission is conditional on a valid no-show fee, and its premise fails on POL-NS-23, so DRIVER_COMPENSATION does not apply.
